 ATTN Michiganders: Election Day is Coming Up! 
 ATTN Michiganders: Election Day is Coming Up! 
 Share: 
 Type:  News 
 If you still need to register (or update your registration) and vote, make a plan to do it this weekend! All local clerks must be open for at least eight hours this weekend for voter registration and in-person absentee voting.    
  At this point, the only way to register to vote in the November 3 Election is in person at your city or township clerk’s office with proof of residency (like a utility bill or paycheck). After you register, you can apply for, complete, and submit an absentee ballot in your clerk’s office. To find the location and hours of your local clerk’s office, you can go to mi.gov/vote and click on “ Where are my clerk’s offices .” 
   Statewide early voting for the November 3 General Election will take place from now through Sunday, November 1, for at least eight hours a day. Your early voting site will likely be in a different location and have different hours than your Election Day polling place. To find your early voting site(s) and the hours, visit mi.gov/vote and click on “ Where do I go to Early Vote .” 
   If you have any questions about voting or need to report an issue, call the nonpartisan Election Protection Hotline at (866) OUR-VOTE | (866) 687-8683 or one of the hotlines available in a language other than English for assistance. Promote the Vote Fund is monitoring all Michigan calls to the hotline now through Election Day, and will respond to issues as they arise. 
  Make a plan to register and vote this weekend! All city and township clerks must be open for at least eight hours this weekend for voter registration and in-person absentee voting.   
   If you still need to register to vote or update your voter registration, you can register to vote or update your registration this weekend at your city or township clerk’s office with proof of residency . At this point, the only way to register to vote in the May 6 Election is in person at your city or township clerk’s office or satellite office with proof of residency (like a utility bill or paycheck). After you register, you can apply for, complete, and submit an absentee ballot in your clerk’s office. To find the location and hours of your local clerk’s office, you can go to mi.gov/vote and click on “ Where are my clerk’s offices .” 
   If you encounter any problems or have questions about voting, call the nonpartisan Election Protection Hotline: (866) OUR-VOTE | (866) 687-8683. (For nonpartisan election protection hotlines in other languages, click here .)
